title: Explore recording rules on Grafana Play (preview)

blocks.content: Explore recording rules on Grafana Play to see how to find recording rules, how the two types differ, and which parts make up one recording rule. You don't change anything.
Explore the **Alert rules** page to see how recording rules are listed.
Go to **Alert rules**.
Recording rules and alert rules are listed on the same page.
Find the **Type** filter. Its options are **All**, **Alert rule**, and **Recording rule**.
Select **Recording rule**. The list now shows only recording rules.
Notice the search box. It now holds `type:recording`, the filter you selected.
Each recording rule in the list computes the result of a query ahead of time, on a schedule, and saves it as a recorded metric.
Recording rules and alert rules share the **Alert rules** page, and the **Type** filter separates them.
Explore the **Rule source** filter to see how the two types of recording rule differ.

blocks.title: See the two types of recording rule

blocks.content: Go to the **Alert rules** page, if you aren't already on it.
In the **Type** filter, select **Recording rule**, if it isn't already selected.
Find the **Rule source** filter. Its options are **All**, **Grafana managed**, and **Data source managed**.
Select **Data source managed**. The list now shows only data source-managed recording rules.
A data source-managed recording rule can query data sources such as Mimir or Loki.
Select **Grafana managed**. The list now shows only Grafana-managed recording rules.
A Grafana-managed recording rule can query a wide range of data sources. This type is recommended and is enabled by default in Grafana Cloud.
A recording rule is either Grafana-managed or data source-managed, and the **Rule source** filter shows one type at a time.
Explore one Grafana-managed recording rule to see the parts that make it up.
Go to the **Alert rules** page, filtered to recording rules.
In the search box, enter `asserts:kpi:feo11y_latency:p75 - Frontend/lcp`, then press Enter. The list now shows only that rule.
Click **asserts:kpi:feo11y_latency:p75 - Frontend/lcp** to open this Grafana-managed recording rule.
Focus on the rule name at the top of the page.
A recording rule has two names. The rule name identifies the recording rule.
Find **Metric name**.

The metric name identifies the recorded metric. Dashboards and alert rules query the recorded metric by this name. This rule's metric name is `asserts:kpi:feo11y_latency:p75`, which is different from the rule name.
Notice **Evaluation interval**.
The evaluation interval is how often a recording rule is evaluated. This rule is evaluated every minute. Each evaluation writes one new data point to the recorded metric.
View the query. The name above the query is the data source the rule queries.
The data source the rule queries is where the rule reads the raw data. This rule reads from `grafanacloud-play-logs`, a logs data source.
Find **Target data source**.
The target data source is where the rule writes the recorded metric. This rule writes to `grafanacloud-play-prom`, so it reads from one data source and writes to another.
A recording rule has a rule name, a metric name, an evaluation interval, a data source it queries, and a target data source.
